raw_case_text:
A 5.5-year-old girl presented with six-day fever up to 38.5 C with spikes mostly in the afternoon, accompanied by pain at the right wrist joint and right elbow joint. The girl's parents are stockbreeders and homemade dairy products had been offered to the child. Three days prior to her admission in our department, she was examined in another hospital, where no remarkable findings from the joints or other systems were noted. As shown in Table 1, laboratory tests were white blood cells 7.2 x 109/L, platelets 180 x 109/L, hemoglobin 131 g/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 19 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) 10 mg/L, monotest negative, alanine aminotransferase (AST) 62 U/L, positive Wright agglutination reaction (title 1/1280), and negative Rose Bengal. Based on the symptoms and the positive Wright reaction, treatment for brucellosis was initiated. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX) (10 mg/kg/day) and rifampicin (15 mg/kg/day) were administered orally.
On the third day of treatment, generalized purpuric lesions were noted accompanied with severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3 x 109/L) and the child was referred to our hospital. On admission the child was febrile (38.8 C) and generalized petechial/purpuric rash, bruising, wet purpura on the palate, and gingival bleeding were noted, while the spleen and the liver were palpable 2 cm below the subcostal margin at the midclavicular line. Examination of the joints and the other systems did not reveal any pathological signs.
Laboratory tests showed white blood cells 7.5 x 109/L (neutrophils 45%, lymphocytes 52%, and monocytes 3%), platelets 1 x 109/L, hemoglobin 120 g/L, ESR 15 mm/h, CRP 7 mg/L, AST 64 U/L, urea 4.1 mmol/L, creatinine 92 mumol/L, and total bilirubin 12 mumol/L. Wright agglutination reaction was positive (title 1/1280), as well as the specific IgM, IgA antibodies against Brucella melitensis. The specific IgG antibodies were negative. Blood cultures were sterile. Direct and indirect Coombs were negative. The quantification of immunoglobulins IgG, IgM, and IgA and complements C3 and C4 was within normal range. Antinuclear antibodies, anti-double stranded DNA antibodies, and rheumatoid factor were negative, while the antiplatelet antibody test was positive. Clotting time and fibrinogen were normal (Table 1).
Due to the very low platelet count and the mucous membrane hemorrhage, treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) (1 gr/kg/day for two days) was initiated, combined with antibiotic therapy with amikacin intravenously (15 mg/kg/day for seven days) and oral rifampicin. TMP/SMX treatment was stopped due to the suspicion of drug-induced thrombocytopenia.
The patient responded with a gradual increase in the number of platelets up to 218 x 109/L five days after treatment. At this stage, oral TMP/SMX administration was reinitiated, without any negative effect on the platelet count. On the contrary, a rise in platelet number up to 503 x 109/L was observed. Fever resolved at the second day of treatment and no new bleeding manifestations appeared. The patient was discharged with rifampicin and TMP/SMX as maintenance therapy for a total six-week treatment. She completed the treatment without further complications and during the regular follow-up platelet counts were normal (Table 1).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 5.5-year-old girl presented with a 6-day history of fever up to 38.5 °C, right wrist and right elbow joint pain, and acute onset of generalized purpuric rash and mucosal bleeding.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 6-day history of fever up to 38.5 °C with afternoon spikes, accompanied by pain in the right wrist and right elbow joints. Three days prior to admission, she was evaluated at an outside hospital, found to have joint pain and initiated on oral trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX) and rifampicin. On the third day of treatment, she developed generalized purpuric lesions and severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3 x 109/L), prompting referral with active mucosal bleeding (palatal wet purpura and gingival bleeding).
subjective.past_medical_history: Evaluated at an outside hospital 3 days prior to admission where no initial joint or systemic findings were noted; started on oral TMP/SMX and rifampicin. Epidemiological history: parents are stockbreeders, and the child was fed homemade unpasteurized dairy products.
subjective.review_of_systems: Petechial/purpuric rash, bruising, wet purpura on palate, gingival bleeding, right wrist and elbow arthralgia. Home medications: TMP/SMX (10 mg/kg/day) and rifampicin (15 mg/kg/day). Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 38.8 °C. Skin and mucous membranes: generalized petechial/purpuric rash, bruising, wet purpura on the palate, and gingival bleeding. Abdomen: spleen and liver palpable 2 cm below the subcostal margin at the midclavicular line (hepatosplenomegaly). Examination of the joints and other systems revealed no pathological signs.
objective.routine_investigations: Outside hospital labs: WBC 7.2 x 109/L, platelets 180 x 109/L, hemoglobin 131 g/L, ESR 19 mm/h, CRP 10 mg/L, AST 62 U/L, Monotest negative. Admission labs: WBC 7.5 x 109/L (45% neutrophils, 52% lymphocytes, 3% monocytes), platelets 1 x 109/L, hemoglobin 120 g/L, ESR 15 mm/h, CRP 7 mg/L, AST 64 U/L, urea 4.1 mmol/L, creatinine 92 mumol/L, total bilirubin 12 mumol/L. Coagulation: clotting time and fibrinogen normal. Autoimmune and serology: direct and indirect Coombs tests negative; IgG, IgM, IgA, C3, and C4 normal; ANA, anti-dsDNA, and rheumatoid factor negative; antiplatelet antibody test was positive.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute brucellosis complicated by severe immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) and peripheral arthritis. Confirmed by Wright agglutination reaction positive at 1/1280 titer (Rose Bengal negative initially), and positive specific IgM and IgA antibodies against Brucella melitensis (specific IgG negative). Blood cultures were sterile. Autoimmune vasculitis, EBV mononucleosis, and consumptive coagulopathy ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Initial TMP/SMX was withheld due to suspicion of drug-induced thrombocytopenia. Treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG 1 g/kg/day for 2 days), IV amikacin (15 mg/kg/day for 7 days), and oral rifampicin (15 mg/kg/day). Platelet count increased to 218 x 109/L after 5 days. Oral TMP/SMX was safely reintroduced without adverse effect on platelets, which rose to 503 x 109/L. Fever resolved on day 2. Discharged on oral rifampicin and TMP/SMX to complete a 6-week course with complete recovery and normal platelet counts on follow-up.
